Auth is compiler-aware

Signed sessions (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age matched to the server-side TTL), PBKDF2 passwords, RBAC policies, session rotation, magic links, TOTP, OAuth/OIDC clients, and WebAuthn verification. Security boundaries feed placement: auth-gated code stays server-side. In production behind HTTPS pass secure=True so cookies also carry Secure — pyweb serve warns at startup when auth is enabled on a non-local host without it (PYWEB_COOKIE_SECURE=1).

@app.page("/dashboard")
@auth.required
def dashboard(): ...

@permission("admin")
def delete_user(uid: int): ...

pyweb check app.pyweb   # secret-leak + vulnerability scan in CI
XSS (escaped templates) / SQLi (parameterized only) / CSRF (tokens + SameSite) / uploads (type/size validation + safe paths) / secret leak (compile error, not warning).

Threat model

ThreatMitigationVerified by
Secret shipped to browserPlacement pins secrets server-side; leak is a compile errorpyweb check in CI
Session theftSigned, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies; rotation on privilege changeauth tests
CSRFPer-session tokens on mutations + SameSite cookiesform tests
Open redirectAllow-list validated next parametersattack-case tests
Path traversalsafe_join containment on uploads/staticattack-case tests
SSRFEgress allow-list on server fetchscan tests
